title: Gluing basis clopens and comparing the affine generic component quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $\eta$ be its generic point, let $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ be its function field, and let $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ be the generic inclusion. Let $u:U\to X$ be any morphism with $U$ affine [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $U_\eta=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $i:U_\eta\to U$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a family of affine open subschemes of $U$ forming an open basis: for every $x\in O$ with $O\subseteq|U|$ open there is $W\in\mathcal B$ with $x\in|W|\subseteq O$. Write $W_\eta=W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k=i^{-1}(W)$ for $W\in\mathcal B$, and suppose that $i_W^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(W)\to\operatorname{Clop}(W_\eta)$ is bijective for every $W\in\mathcal B$. Here clopen means both open and closed. Then $j$ and $i$ are affine morphisms (the inverse image of every affine open is affine), $U_\eta$ is affine, and both $|U|$ and $|U_\eta|$ are spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space]. Inverse image $i^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(U)\to\operatorname{Clop}(U_\eta)$ is bijective. For a space $T$ write $q_T:|T|\to\pi_0(T)$ for the quotient by belonging to the same connected component, a maximal connected subset, endowed with the quotient topology. The induced map $h=\pi_0(i):\pi_0(U_\eta)\to\pi_0(U)$ is a homeomorphism satisfying $h\circ q_{U_\eta}=q_U\circ i$. No affineness of intersections of basis opens or quasi-separatedness of $X$ is assumed. Empty $U$ and the empty basis for it are allowed.

proof.text: For an affine open $V\subseteq X$, its inverse image under $j$ is either empty or all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$: the spectrum of a field has one point, mapping to $\eta$. Both are affine (the empty scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$). Thus $j$ is affine by the definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. This tests every affine open separately and imposes no condition on intersections or on $X$.

The projection $i$ is the base change of $j$ along $u$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1) to get that $i$ is affine and (2), since $U$ is affine, to get that $U_\eta$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] both $U$ and $U_\eta$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] to each: their underlying spaces are spectral.

proof.text: Fix a clopen $D\subseteq U_\eta$. For each $W\in\mathcal B$, the hypothesis gives a unique clopen $C_W\subseteq W$ with $i_W^{-1}C_W=D\cap W_\eta$. If $B\in\mathcal B$ lies in $W\cap V$ for $W,V\in\mathcal B$, then $C_W\cap B$ and $C_V\cap B$ are clopen in $B$, and both pull back to $D\cap B_\eta$. Injectivity for $B$ makes them equal. For every point of $W\cap V$ there is such a $B$ containing it, by the basis property. Hence $C_W\cap V=C_V\cap W$. No affineness of $W\cap V$ was used.

proof.text: Put $C=\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal B}C_W$. Agreement on overlaps gives $C\cap W=C_W$ for every $W$: a point in $C\cap W$ belongs to some $C_V$, hence to $C_W$. Each $C_W$ is open in $U$, and $U\setminus C=\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal B}(W\setminus C_W)$ is open as well. Thus $C$ is clopen. Finally $i^{-1}C=\bigcup_W(D\cap W_\eta)=D$, since the basis covers $U$ and its inverse images cover $U_\eta$. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), normal generic restriction auxiliary argument of lem-sfb-normal-generic-continuous-sections, component-comparison clause; agent expansion; explicit union and complementary union construction

proof.text: If clopens $C,C^\prime\subseteq U$ have equal inverse images, then $C\cap W$ and $C^\prime\cap W$ have equal inverse images in $W_\eta$ for every $W\in\mathcal B$. Local injectivity gives equality of these restrictions. Taking their unions over the basis gives $C=C^\prime$. Inverse image preserves clopens because $i$ is continuous, so it is the asserted bijection. The union arguments also cover empty $U$ and an empty basis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-spectral-clopen-component-homeomorphism] with $T=|U_\eta|$, $S=|U|$, and the continuous underlying map of $i$. Step 2 supplies spectrality and steps 3–5 supply the clopen inverse-image bijection. It gives precisely the induced homeomorphism $h=\pi_0(i)$ and the equality $h\circ q_{U_\eta}=q_U\circ i$, including empty spaces.
